title: Letter to Joseph Hooker on the abominable mystery
claim: Called the sudden appearance and rapid spread of the higher plants in the Cretaceous an abominable mystery, and wondered whether they had evolved for a long time somewhere unsampled.
note: The framing question for everything below.

title: On the origin of angiosperms
claim: The flower began as a bisexual cone like those of Bennettitales (the anthostrobilus); the euanthial theory.
note: Bennettitales are no longer thought close, but the flower-as-shoot idea survives.

title: The Caytoniales, a new group of angiospermous plants from the Jurassic rocks of Yorkshire
claim: Caytonia's closed cupules looked like carpels; first proposed as Jurassic angiosperms, soon shown to be seed ferns.
note: Not angiosperms, but caytonialean cupules returned as a model for the second integument (Doyle; Shi et al. 2021).

title: A theory of angiosperm evolution
claim: Angiosperms arose in Permian or Triassic tropical uplands, where they left no fossils, and only later reached the lowlands.
note: The upland refuge has never been demonstrated; long clock ages revived the question of a hidden early history.

title: How old are the angiosperms?
claim: Reviewed every claimed pre-Cretaceous angiosperm and found none reliable.
note: Herendeen et al. (2017) revisited this review and reached the same verdict.

title: Palynological evidence on early differentiation of angiosperms
claim: The pollen record shows monosulcate grains first in the Early Cretaceous, then tricolpates, then a steady rise.
note: Muller's 1981 review (on the time tree) followed this.

title: Flowering plants: evolution above the species level
claim: Proposed that the outer integument of the angiosperm ovule is a cupule, as in glossopterids and other Mesozoic seed plants; favoured origin in seasonally dry, open habitats.
note: The cupule homology was revived by Doyle and by Shi et al. (2021).

title: Early Cretaceous fossil evidence for angiosperm evolution
claim: Potomac Group leaves begin small with loosely organised venation, on stream margins, then diversify alongside tricolpate pollen through the Albian.
note: The leaf-pollen succession is still the classic model of the early radiation.

title: Palaeo-succession of earliest angiosperm evolution
claim: Columellate semi-tectate pollen enters the English Wealden in the presumed Barremian; doubted that angiosperms were monophyletic.
note: His Wealden entry was later moved into the late Hauterivian (Hughes & McDougall 1987, 1990).

title: Barremian earliest angiosperm pollen
claim: Named the Wealden grains: angiospermid pollen under 1% of Barremian assemblages and usually under 25 micrometres.
note: Ages revised downward by Hughes & McDougall.

title: Arguments for a glossopterid ancestry of angiosperms
claim: Glossopterid seed-bearing organs could be the precursor of the carpel and outer integument.
note: Glossopterids recur among proposed angiophytes but no sister group is agreed.

title: Phylogenetic analysis of seed plants and the origin of angiosperms
claim: Cladistics placed angiosperms with Bennettitales, Pentoxylon and Gnetales: the anthophytes.
note: Molecular trees from 1999-2000 put Gnetales with conifers, dissolving the anthophytes.

title: Seed plant phylogeny and the origin of angiosperms
claim: The angiosperm line was separate by the Triassic, though its modern features need not be that old.
note: Stem-versus-crown thinking from here on frames the age debate.

title: The leaf venation and reproductive structures of a Late Triassic angiosperm, Sanmiguelia lewisii
claim: Argued that Sanmiguelia from the Late Triassic was an angiosperm; later (1989) described angiosperm-like Crinopolles pollen from the Triassic of Virginia.
note: Not accepted as angiosperm; the pollen are treated as a separate, extinct group.

title: Records of angiospermid pollen entry into the English Early Cretaceous succession
claim: Moved the first English angiospermid pollen into the late Hauterivian.
note: Confirmed by Hughes, McDougall & Chapman (1991).

title: Quantitative analyses of the early angiosperm radiation
claim: Counting Cretaceous floras showed angiosperms widely dominant, at least in the Northern Hemisphere, by about 90 Ma.
note: Started the quantitative study of the Cretaceous radiation.

title: Angiospermous pollen (monosulcate-trichotomosulcate phase) from the very early Lower Cretaceous of Southern Tuscany
claim: Reported Valanginian-Hauterivian angiosperm pollen from Italy.
note: A conference abstract only; widely cited for the Valanginian entry.

title: Molecular evidence for pre-Cretaceous angiosperm origins
claim: A strict GAPDH clock dated the monocot-dicot split to the Carboniferous (about 319 Ma) and the dicot subclasses to the Permian.
note: Criticised at once for method; started the clock-versus-fossil conflict.

title: Exceptional new record of Cretaceous Hauterivian angiospermid pollen from southern England
claim: Ten grains of one tectate-columellate monosulcate type from a single late Hauterivian sample: the oldest generally accepted angiospermid pollen.
note: On the time tree as Hauterivian-colthick.

title: Phylogenetic evidence for the herbaceous origin of angiosperms
claim: The first angiosperms were small rhizomatous herbs (the paleoherb hypothesis).
note: Amborella and Austrobaileyales as early branches favoured woody ancestors; aquatic and herbaceous habits arose early too.

title: Phylogenies and angiosperm diversification
claim: Several basic clades were present by the Barremian-Aptian, so the crown began diversifying then, not necessarily much earlier; the stem (angiophytes) may reach the Late Triassic.

title: The enigma of angiosperm origins
claim: Only the whole fossil record, above all dispersed pollen in dated successions, can solve the origin; set out phases of entry from the Hauterivian.

title: Evidence for the earliest stage of angiosperm pollen evolution: a paleoequatorial section from Israel
claim: In Israel the sequence begins with small inaperturate columellate grains in the late Valanginian and ends with tricolpates and monoporates in the Aptian.
note: With Trevisan, the basis for a Valanginian start in northern Gondwana.

title: In search of the first flower: a Jurassic angiosperm, Archaefructus
claim: Described Archaefructus from the Yixian Formation of China as Late Jurassic.
note: The Yixian beds were redated to the Early Cretaceous (about 125 Ma); Sun et al. 2002 named the family Archaefructaceae.

authors: Mathews & Donoghue; Qiu et al.; Soltis et al.; Parkinson et al.
title: Amborella identified as sister to all other living angiosperms
claim: Independent DNA studies placed Amborella, then water lilies and Austrobaileyales, at the base of the living angiosperms.
note: Fixed the root that every later dating and ecology study uses.

authors: Bowe et al.; Chaw et al.
title: Gnetales grouped with conifers
claim: Molecular trees put Gnetales with or within conifers, not with angiosperms.
note: Ended the anthophyte hypothesis; living gymnosperms offer no sister to angiosperms.

title: Dark and disturbed: a new image of early angiosperm ecology
claim: Early-branching living angiosperms suggest the first angiosperms were woody plants of dim, disturbed, wet forest understories; water lilies an early aquatic radiation.

title: A boreal early cradle of angiosperms? Angiosperm-like pollen from the Middle Triassic of the Barents Sea
claim: Columellate monosulcate angiosperm-like pollen in the Middle Triassic, about 100 million years before the accepted record.
note: Authors themselves suggest a stem group; reviewers doubt angiosperm affinity.

title: The age and diversification of the angiosperms re-revisited
claim: A relaxed clock with 36 fossil calibrations dated the angiosperms to 167-199 Ma.

title: An uncorrelated relaxed-clock analysis suggests an earlier origin for flowering plants
claim: Crown angiosperms centred on the Late Triassic, much older than their fossils.
note: Range here is the Late Triassic, not the paper's exact interval.

title: Early flowers and angiosperm evolution
claim: Thousands of tiny charcoalified Early Cretaceous flowers from Portugal and North America show diverse basal lineages by the Barremian-Aptian.

title: Molecular and fossil evidence on the origin of angiosperms
claim: Review: the origin of angiosperm features is still unsolved; candidate relatives are extinct seed plants with cupules.

title: Angiosperm-like pollen and Afropollis from the Middle Triassic (Anisian) of the Germanic Basin
claim: Six types of angiosperm-like pollen from the Anisian of Switzerland, about 243 Ma, interpreted as an angiosperm stem group.
note: Differs from Cretaceous grains in its very thin nexine.

title: A metacalibrated time-tree documents the early rise of flowering plant phylogenetic diversity
claim: Bounding the crown age with the fossil record gave an Early Cretaceous crown, estimated with high confidence.
note: The value 139 Ma is from memory; check.

title: Heterogeneous rates of molecular evolution and diversification could explain the Triassic age estimate for angiosperms
claim: Shifts in rates of molecular evolution and diversification can make clocks overestimate the angiosperm age.

title: Montsechia, an ancient aquatic angiosperm
claim: Montsechia from Barremian lake limestones of Spain lived and reproduced under water, like Ceratophyllum.
note: Earliest well-known angiosperm macrofossil.

title: Palaeobotanical redux: revisiting the age of the angiosperms
claim: Re-examined Triassic and Jurassic claims: none is proven; unequivocal angiosperms begin in the Valanginian-Hauterivian.

title: Constraining uncertainty in the timescale of angiosperm evolution and the veracity of a Cretaceous Terrestrial Revolution
claim: Rejected a post-Jurassic origin; the cryptic early history could be anywhere from 23 to 121 million years long.
note: Range derived from the abstract's 23-121 Myr gap before the ~130 Ma record.

title: Origin of angiosperms and the puzzle of the Jurassic gap
claim: Plastid genomes of about 2,350 species with 62 calibrations dated the crown to about 209 Ma, leaving a Jurassic gap.

title: How deep is the conflict between molecular and fossil evidence on the age of angiosperms?
claim: Monosulcate pollen appears first in northern Gondwana in the Valanginian; the pollen sequence matches the molecular tree but not Triassic clock ages; a restricted Late Jurassic presence is possible.

title: The delayed and geographically heterogeneous diversification of flowering plant families
claim: Families typically waited tens of millions of years (37-56 Myr on average) between their origin and the diversification of living species; angiosperm-dominated biomes came only in the Palaeocene.
note: Author list from memory; check.

title: Fossil data support a pre-Cretaceous origin of flowering plants
claim: Modelling incomplete sampling of fossils assigned to living families put several family origins in the Jurassic.
note: Budd, Mann, Doyle, Coiro & Hilton (2021) argued the conclusion is unsound.

title: Mesozoic cupules and the origin of the angiosperm second integument
claim: Recurved cupules from an Early Cretaceous silicified peat in Inner Mongolia match the second integument; several Mesozoic groups are angiosperm relatives (angiophytes).
note: A partial answer to the ancestry question, from a peat.

title: Extinction at the end-Cretaceous and the origin of modern Neotropical rainforests
claim: In Colombia plant diversity fell 45% at the K-Pg boundary and took about 6 million years to recover; Palaeocene forests were angiosperm-dominated, closed-canopy rainforests.

title: No phylogenetic evidence for angiosperm mass extinction at the K-Pg boundary
claim: Mega-phylogenies of 32,000-73,000 species show steady extinction rates and no K-Pg mass extinction of lineages.
note: Hagen (2024) argued the methods lack power to detect one; species-level losses in the fossils are not denied.

title: Ad fontes: divergence-time estimation and the age of angiosperms
claim: Old clock ages are artefacts of rate shifts tied to repeated life-history changes.
note: Title paraphrased; check.

title: A molecular temporal evolutionary framework of land plants and the age of angiosperms
claim: Crown angiosperms about 220 Ma (95% HPD 184-257).

title: New insights on angiosperm crown age based on Bayesian node dating and skyline fossilized birth-death approaches
claim: A largely Triassic crown age, 255-202 Ma.

title: Uncertainty in the timing of diversification of flowering plants rests with equivocal interpretation of their fossil record
claim: Without the doubtful older fossils as calibrations, crown angiosperms date to the Late Jurassic-Early Cretaceous; clocks can recover an explosive radiation.
